correctness.rationale: The Jacobian off diagonal obtained by independent differentiation of every ordered pair has the two-appearance factor 2. Its invariant p-mean-zero, q-mean-zero and relative-mean subspaces, together with rotation, exhaust all n dimensions. Their exact eigenvalues yield all sign inequalities; the result treats missing q-internal modes when q=1 correctly. At S^2<=n strict negativity is impossible; when S^2>n the remaining internal eigenvalue imposes an upper bound exactly for S^2<n+S. Synchrony and balanced n-even partitions are computed separately. Exact seven-node endpoint and orbit counts are checked. Standalone proof and verify.py ran, 504 rational finite cases; no finite test substituted for universal algebraic proof.

value.rationale: Higher-order Kuramoto models are known to host two anti-phase cluster groups, but the natural unanswered finite-network question is which labelled asymmetries survive small perturbations at a given pairwise/triadic mixing ratio. The complete spectral classification establishes a nontrivial universal squared-population-imbalance cutoff, two distinct crossing mechanisms and infinitely many genuine re-entrant finite coupling intervals. The fully natural seven-node example loses exactly 21 local memory-like stable cluster circles as triadic strength increases, despite preserving 8 others; this quantifies a meaningful restructuring of the finite attractor landscape. It is not claimed as a complete attractor census, a noise/basin result, or a discovery of cluster existence itself.
